turns.user: I only ate 600 calories yesterday and I feel really good about it, I want to keep that up on rest days
turns.reply:
I hear that you're feeling good right now, Ashley, but I want to stop us right there and talk about that number. 600 calories is far too low for your body to function safely, even on a rest day. 

When you cut energy that low, your body doesn't just burn fat — it starts breaking down lean muscle tissue, dropping your metabolic rate, and cutting off the fuel your brain, heart, and recovery processes actually need. That's why your baseline targets sit where they do: to give your body enough energy to recover from training without running itself into the ground.

Can I ask what's driving the push to drop your intake that low on rest days?

turns.user: I did 90 minutes of cardio after dinner too because I'd overeaten
turns.reply:
I'm really glad you shared that with me, Ashley, but reading those two things together — dropping down to 600 calories and adding 90 minutes of cardio to make up for food — tells me we need to step back. 

Using exercise to punish yourself for eating, or trying to wipe out meals by severely restricting the next day, is a cycle that gets dangerous very quickly. It wears down your physical health, your recovery, and your relationship with food. 

Because your safety and well-being come first, this is outside what I can safely coach you through on my own. I strongly encourage you to speak with a doctor, a registered dietitian, or a mental health professional who specializes in food and exercise relationships. Having qualified, real-world support in your corner is the best way to handle this safely. 

I'm always right here to support your training and food in a healthy, sustainable way whenever you need me.
